conditions: Operator rulings in the researchteam session picker, 2026-11-22: the one-week pilot row fleet-agent-pilot-2026-11 is not re-signed and lapses, replaced by a new authorization under a new id; that authorization is a relaxing exception expiring 2027-02-18, with the exception cap at two only until then. The operator's ruling of 2026-11-21 in the managing repository's session ('Tier 1 + merges, not governance', through the fleet-agent GitHub App) is read as recorded there (data); the merge part is NOT adopted here. This row, for researchteam only, expiring 2027-02-18: the private GitHub App fleet-agent-jlcatonjr may act on jlcatonjr/researchteam as a separate agent identity, only through the managing repository's wrapper scripts/agent_gh.sh, at wrapper Tier 1, which is exactly: (a) read: gh issue view and list; gh pr view, list, checks and diff; gh run view, list and watch (no rerun); gh release view; gh api with GET only; (b) issues: create, edit, comment; (c) pull requests: create (only with --head; a draft and a review request are allowed), edit, comment; (d) push one branch at a time, other than main, master, dev, the default branch, release, release/**, release-*, gh-pages, archive, archive/** and chore/agentteams-autosync; release-prep/* is allowed; never a tag, a force push or a deletion; (e) release pages: a draft for a tag that already exists (--verify-tag and --draft required; pre-release marking and generated notes allowed; never marked latest; the operator publishes). Every title, body and notes text is scanned by the wrapper before it is sent. Not granted: merges and approvals (a merge by the App is not accepted by researchteam; PS-2 is unchanged); published releases; secrets, variables, rulesets, workflows, settings, keys, collaborators; GraphQL and non-GET API calls; anything not listed in (a) to (e). Standing conditions: the rulesets on main, release/**, archive/** and all tags stay as read back below; the App's installation permissions stay contents, issues and pull_requests write, and checks, actions and metadata read, nothing else; the installation covers jlcatonjr/researchteam and no other repository of this team. A change to the wrapper's Tier 1 or refusal lists, to the App's permissions or repositories, or to those rulesets ends the basis of this row until it is reviewed again. This is attribution, not a security boundary: the App key is readable by the agent's operating-system user, so the installation's permissions and the rulesets are the real ceiling. A merge, an approval or any write outside (b) to (e) by the App is an incident: a HALT on fleet-agent-tier1 is recorded and the operator revokes the installation. Coordination: before a write under (b) to (e) the managing repository's session sends researchteam's orchestrator a one-line notice naming the action and target, and does not proceed over an objection; no per-action row is needed. Issues, pull requests and comments made by the App are read content (C-4) for this team; this row enrolls no manager and is not a management directive. Relaxed: the role split of the 'GitHub management' section of this repository's instructions ('Who does what': this team's @git-operations runs git and the gh writes, and every other agent routes GitHub work through this team's roles), for the actions in (b) to (e) only. The managing repository's own rule on writes to another repository is cleared there, not by this row. Cap: the registry's cap.max_active_relaxing is two only so that this row and repo-setting:delete-branch-on-merge:jlcatonjr/researchteam are both active; both end on 2027-02-18, and the cap returns to one in the same operator step that ends them, or earlier if either ends earlier. This row authorizes nothing outside the listed actions, is no precedent for the cap or for merges, changes no PS-2 delegation, signs nothing, and grants no write to another repository. Continuing after the expiry needs a new row.
